matrix.legacySemantics: The plugin discovers supported child widgets and manages direction, disabled state, and corners.

matrix.legacySemantics: A list plugin adds menu roles, focus management, submenu behavior, and callbacks.

matrix.legacySemantics: A div-based plugin renders determinate or indeterminate progress and change events.

matrix.legacySemantics: A Widget Factory base class normalizes mouse capture, distance, delay, start, drag, and stop hooks.

matrix.legacySemantics: Arbitrary elements receive handles, constraints, helpers, animation, and resize callbacks.

results.evidence: Both slices repeat state changes, but they do not require the same bounded facade: the editor needs dialog/tabs/form/sortable behavior while the toolbar needs menu/tooltip/roving-focus behavior.
The adapter sketch saves 13 of 164 lines (7.9%) in the editor and 7 of 91 lines (7.7%) in the toolbar, below both the 25% and 20-line thresholds.
Direct migration is tested, but an unimplemented adapter has no executable keyboard, focus, form, touch, forced-color, reduced-motion, or no-script proof.
Covering both slices would require at least dialog, tabs, sortable, menu, and tooltip facades, exceeding the two-widget limit before option, method, and event compatibility is considered.
The 2870-byte minified sketch is under the minified limit but has no measured gzip artifact; missing evidence is a failure. Direct migration adds no adapter bytes or jQuery UI runtime.
A facade would need to translate imperative initialization and calls across multiple independent roots, creating a second lifecycle boundary without removing direct migration work.
No adapter implementation, exact public types, 100% changed-line coverage, or three-browser package gate exists. Ticket 0039 intentionally ships none.
Any future bounded adapter would be experimental and removable before 1.0, while direct native migration remains documented.
No adapter ships, so native jQStar markup, methods, events, state attributes, CSS, and accessibility behavior remain unchanged.

requirements: pointer capture bounded to one semantic operation
genericInteractions.reason: No two independent native jQStar consumers require a generic arbitrary-element draggable primitive.
No two independent native consumers require a shared drop-target coordinator.
One bounded recipe already owns panel resizing; one consumer does not justify a generic interaction API.
Existing native controls cover current selection tasks and no pair of consumers requires lasso behavior.
The bounded sortable recipe serves its current task; no second independent need supports extracting a generic primitive.
